FN is a direct optical module manufacturing and advanced optical packaging read-through, but later layers must test customer concentration, margin capture, and whether it has true bottleneck power or mainly pass-through EMS exposure.
COHR and LITE should be treated as reference optical-component leaders, not alpha-discovery names, because they anchor lasers, InP capacity, silicon photonics, and datacom transceiver context.

US-listed coverage of pure epitaxy equipment for InP/compound-semiconductor optical capacity is thin; Aixtron appears relevant from external context but is not a primary US exchange-listed common stock candidate in this pass.

AXTI should remain the primary underfollowed Layer 1B candidate for the InP substrate layer; next layer must verify InP revenue mix, non-China capacity, export-control exposure and customer qualification evidence.
LITE and COHR are better used as reference comparables for laser/InP demand and pricing power rather than as the main underfollowed discovery lane, because market attention appears high.

MTSI is a viable underfollowed component candidate around 1.6T optical links because it combines CW lasers, photodetectors and high-speed optical connectivity products, but materiality to consolidated revenue remains the key evidence gap.

FN is a capacity and qualification-cycle candidate in optical packaging and precision manufacturing; it is not a laser/substrate chokepoint, so keep it as a second-order beneficiary unless datacom optical manufacturing constraints are proven.

US-listed pure-play epitaxy equipment exposure appears limited; Aixtron is a strong tool-layer reference but is not a primary US-listed exchange candidate, so later passes should decide whether ADR/OTC or non-US listings are allowed.

AXTI should be tracked as the cleanest US-listed InP substrate candidate for the optical compound-semiconductor stack; survival depends on evidence that AI optical demand reaches AXTI revenue/backlog rather than staying at the narrative level.
MTSI is not small-cap but is an underfollowed-by-theme component-layer candidate because its 1.6T CW laser and silicon-photonics products sit below AI networking headlines.

POET belongs in speculative_shadow: direct AI optical-engine language and capacity expansion are attractive, but customer qualification, revenue conversion, yield and dilution must be verified before upgrade.
LITE and COHR should be retained as reference anchors for demand validation and pricing/attention checks, but not allowed to crowd out substrate, epitaxy, tool and integration candidates.

Next Layer 1B pass should search US-listed or US-traded ADR/OTC names in epitaxy equipment and inspection/test gates, including whether Aixtron has a usable US-traded ADR and whether any US-listed metrology/test vendors have optical/compound-semiconductor exposure.

AXTI should be tracked as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed InP substrate candidate for the optical compound-semiconductor stack; key gating evidence is InP revenue mix, export permits, and data-center customer qualification.
TSEM should be tracked as a silicon photonics foundry capacity candidate with named 1.6T AI optical relationships, including NVIDIA and Innolight-related announcements.
MTSI should be tracked as a less obvious optical-component and signal-integrity supplier for 1.6T/3.2T modules, especially CW lasers, modulator drivers and TIAs.

The chokepoint map should separate four layers: InP substrates, epitaxy/wafer processing, laser/photonic components, and module/transceiver assembly; underfollowed alpha is more likely in the first three than in obvious module assemblers.
Need next pass on non-US or OTC names for epitaxy equipment and InP/III-V supply, including Aixtron and Japanese substrate suppliers, because US-listed coverage may miss key bottleneck owners.
